q: Of whom was Jude a servant?
a: Jude was a servant of Jesus Christ.

q: Who was the brother of Jude?
a: James was the brother of Jude.

q: To whom did Jude write?
a: He wrote to those who were called, beloved in God the Father, and kept for Jesus Christ.

q: What did Jude want multiplied to those to whom he wrote?
a: Jude wanted mercy, peace, and love to be multiplied.

q: What did Jude first want to write about?
a: Jude first wanted to write about their common salvation.

q: What did Jude actually write about?
a: Jude actually wrote about the need to struggle for the faith of the saints.

q: How did some condemned and ungodly men come?
a: Some condemned and ungodly men came stealthily.

q: What did the condemned and ungodly men do?
a: They changed the grace of God into sexual immorality and denied Jesus Christ.

q: From where did the Lord once save people?
a: The Lord saved them from the land of Egypt.

q: What did the Lord do to those people who did not believe?
a: The Lord destroyed those people who did not believe.

q: What did the Lord do to the angels who left their proper place?
a: The Lord put them in chains in darkness for judgment.

q: What did Sodom, Gomorrah, and the cities around them do?
a: They fornicated and pursued unnatural desires.

q: Like Sodom, Gomorrah, and the cities around them, what do the condemned and ungodly men do?
a: They pollute their bodies in their dreams, reject authority, and say evil things.

q: What did the archangel Michael say to the devil?
a: The archangel Michael said, “May the Lord rebuke you.”

q: For whom do the condemned and ungodly men shamelessly care?
a: They shamelessly care for themselves.

q: Enoch was which place in line from Adam?
a: Enoch was the seventh in line from Adam.

q: Upon whom will the Lord execute judgment?
a: The Lord will execute judgment upon all people.

q: Who are the ungodly men who will be convicted?
a: Grumblers, complainers, those who go after their evil desires, loud boasters, and those who praise for personal advantage are the ungodly men who will be convicted.

q: Who spoke words in the past about mockers?
a: The apostles of the Lord Jesus Christ spoke words in the past about mockers.

q: What is true of the mockers who go after the own ungodly lusts, who cause divisions and are sensual?
a: They do not have the Holy Spirit.

q: How were the beloved building themselves up and praying?
a: The beloved were building themselves up in their most holy faith, and praying in the Holy Spirit.

q: What were the beloved to keep themselves in and look for?
a: The beloved were to keep themselves in and look for the love of God and the mercy of the Lord Jesus Christ.

q: Who were the beloved supposed to save?
a: The beloved were supposed to save those with a garment spotted by the flesh, and those in the fire.

q: What was God their Savior, through Jesus Christ their Lord, able to do?
a: God was able to keep them from stumbling and place them before the presence of his glory without blemish.

q: What things should be given to the only God our Savior through Jesus Christ our Lord?
a: To the only God our Savior through Jesus Christ our Lord be glory, majesty, power, and authority.

q: When did God have glory?
a: God had glory before all time, now, and forevermore.
